To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of TCDD on hepatic GH signaling and CYP2D expression are dependent on AHR activation, and AHR activation per sé leads to dysregulations of hepatic GH signal transduction components and suppression of selected, but not all STAT5b target gene products.
TCDD suppresses hepatic Cyp2d and Mup2, two STAT5b target gene products, and GH signaling components in a mouse model that is Ahr (-/ -).
AHR activation leads to AHR-dependent suppression of Cyp2d, Mup2, and components of GH signaling in mouse liver, and AHR-dependent induction and suppression of CYP3A, POR, and inflammatory markers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the AHR in mediating the effects of TCDD on hepatic gene regulation, with a focus on GH signaling components.
the physiological role of the AHR in the regulation of hepatic GH signal transduction and metabolism.
the AHR-dependent effects of dioxin on the hepatic GH axis, which may be relevant to dioxin-induced hepatotoxicity and/or hepatocellular carcinoma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AHR is required for the TCDD-mediated suppression of Cyp2d and Mup genes and the TCDD-induced suppression of Cyp1 and induction of Cyp3 genes.
AHR activation leads to suppression of hepatic CYP2D and CYP3A genes and dysregulation of GH signaling components.
AHR activation, in the presence or absence of exogenous ligand, leads to AHR-dependent suppression of hepatic GH receptor, JAK2, and STATs 5a and 5b.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the AHR is a critical regulator of hepatic gene expression, and that TCDD-induced AHR activation leads to AHR-dependent suppression of some GH target genes and to AHR-dependent induction/suppression of hepatic CYP genes.
the AHR is a major regulator of hepatic CYPs, GH signaling components, and MUPs.

TCDD-induced AHR-dependent changes in GH signaling are associated with AHR-dependent changes to Cyp2d expression and that AHR-independent changes in hepatic GH signaling may be involved in AHR-independent effects of TCDD on hepatic Cyp2d and Cyp3a gene expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AHR has physiological roles, and is involved in the suppression of hepatic cytochrome P-450 genes and GH signaling components by TCDD.
the AHR can mediate biological responses that are not directly linked to the induction of Cyp 1a1 and other AHR target genes.
the AHR can mediate biological responses in the absence of xenobiotic exposure.
